xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:DeclarationOfUnmodifiedOpinion: Statement on impact of audit qualification
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:DetailsOfAuditQualificationExp: During the course of our audit, we observed significant deficiencies in the Company's inventory management system. In our opinion, the inventory is overstated by Rs.1,213.79 lakhs, comprising obsolete stock of Rs. 700.84 lakhs, overvaluation of Rs. 194.43 lakhs, and stock shortages of Rs. 318.52 lakhs. Consequently, the profit for the period is also overstated by the same amount.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:AuditQualificationsWhereTheImp: Inventory Management Deficiencies Mismanagement of inventory occurred due to closure of Delhi, Juhu, and Borivali branches, and return of goods without barcoding. Management is refurbishing all stock for further utilization and has tie-ups with TV serial directors to use old refurbished cloths as costumes. Impact of the arrangement will be visible from July onwards. Management will not obsolete the goods but instead utilize them for furtherance of business.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:DetailsOfAuditQualificationExp: Loan agreements for Short Term Loans and Advances given to various parties (Asset) for a total amount of Rs 1,071.88 lakhs were not provided. Out of these loans given, certain parties amounting Rs. 427.59 lakhs, there have been no receipts from these parties in last 2 financial years. In the absence of any agreement and balance confirmations from these parties and in view of no receipts from these parties in past 2 years, we are of the opinion that loans and advances aggregating Rs 427.59 lakhs may not be recoverable by the company. Assets are over stated in the balance sheet to this extent.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:AuditQualificationsWhereTheImp: Loans given to employees and third parties are stated to be fully recoverable. Management has taken initiative to collect old loans and advances and is confident of full recovery in the near future. The advances were given prior to the Covid period, during which parties faced financial difficulties, causing collection delays.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:DetailsOfAuditQualificationExp: Internal Control Processes are not commensurate with the size of the business
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:ManagementsEstimationOnTheImpa: Impact on financial statement is not ascertainable
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:ReasonsIfManagementIsUnableToE: Internal Control process does not require financial impact and Management has already taken remedial steps to control the stock management process.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:AuditorsCommentsOnManagementsE: The management has explained that the matter primarily relates to strengthening of internal control procedures and does not have a directly quantifiable financial impact on the financial statements. We note the management's representation regarding the remedial measures undertaken to improve inventory management and related control processes. However, the effectiveness and sustainability of these measures will be subject to implementation and continued monitoring.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:DetailsOfAuditQualificationExp: During the course of audit, it was noted that the company has not made any provision or estimation for gratuity liability in the financial statements. As per the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, gratuity is a statutory obligation payable to eligible employees upon cessation of employment. The absence of an actuarial valuation or management estimate renders the gratuity liability uncertain and unrecognized. This non-provision may result in understatement of employee benefit obligations and could materially affect the true and fair view of the company's financial position.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:ManagementsEstimationOnTheImpa: Management is in the process of ascertaining the impact of the qualification related to gratuity on financial statement.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:ReasonsIfManagementIsUnableToE: the company is in the process of obtaining an actuarial valuation to estimate gratuity liability. Appropriate provision will be recognized in the financial statements upon completion of this exercise to ensure compliance with statutory requirements and fair presentation.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:AuditorsCommentsOnManagementsE: We note the management's submission that it is in the process of obtaining an actuarial valuation to determine the gratuity liability. Until such valuation is completed and the resulting liability, if any, is recognized in the financial statements, the financial impact of this matter remains unascertained. Appropriate accounting treatment should be considered upon completion of the valuation exercise in accordance with the applicable accounting requirements.
